nodes.name: NF Cleaning
nodes.procedure: The NF (1×2 cm²) was ultrasonically cleaned in acetone, ethanol, and ultra-pure water for 15 min, respectively.
nodes.source_text: the NF (1×2 cm²) was ultrasonically cleaned in acetone, ethanol, and ultra-pure water for 15 min, respectively.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal Synthesis Ni_xFe_{1-x}-LDH@NF
nodes.procedure: The different mole ratios of Ni and Fe (x = 0.3, 0.5 and 0.7) were obtained through mixing Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O and Fe(NO₃)₃·9H₂O where the total number of two metal cations remained at 1.2 mmol (for x=0.3: 0.36 mmol Ni, 0.84 mmol Fe; x=0.5: 0.6 mmol Ni, 0.6 mmol Fe; x=0.7: 0.84 mmol Ni, 0.36 mmol Fe). Afterward, NH₄F (92.5 mg) and urea (360 mg) were added and dissolved in 30 mL DI water to acquire clean solution under constant stirring for 20 min. Subsequently, the pre-cleaned NF and NiFe precursor solution were transferred to a 50 mL stainless-steel Teflon-lined autoclave and heated at 120°C for 5 h. Finally, the Ni_xFe_{1-x}LDH@NF was collected after thoroughly rinsing with DI water and dried in an electric oven at 60°C.

nodes.name: IrO₂@NF Preparation
nodes.procedure: A homogeneous paste was obtained by 10 mg IrO₂ powder, 30 μL of 5 wt% of Nafion and a few drops of ethanol, which was supported on 1 cm×1 cm NF and then pressed at 10 MPa. The as-prepared electrodes were dried at 60°C for 12 h.

nodes.description: OER performance in O2-saturated 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: A standard three-electrode system in O2 saturated 1M KOH was employed... compensation of iRs drop of each polarization curve with 90% was automatically performed... LSV curves were collected at a constant rate of 5mV·s^{-1}... Tafel slopes were given by fitting... EIS was measured at 1.43V versus RHE... C_dl was determined... Ni_{0.3}Fe_{0.7}-LDH@NF displays... ultralow OER overpotentials of 184, 256, 273 and 287mV to achieve 10, 100, 200 and 400mA·cm^{-2}... Tafel slope as small as 56.68mV·dec^{-1}... R_ct of 9.479Ω·cm²... C_dl of 6.66mF·cm^{-2}... nearly 100% FE... voltage applied after the CP test remains almost unchanged.

nodes.characterization_summary: Diffraction peaks at 11.88°, 23.67°, 34.78°, 39.38° and 60.21° match (003), (006), (012), (015) and (110) planes of NiFe LDH (JCPDS No. 49-0188).
nodes.evidence_snippet: the diffraction peaks centered at 11.88°, 23.67°, 34.78°, 39.38° and 60.21° matched well with the (003), (006), (012), (015) and (110) crystal planes of NiFe LDH (JCPDS No. 49-0188)

nodes.characterization_summary: Vibration peaks at 3439, 1631, 1383 and 689 cm⁻¹ assigned to -OH, H₂O, CO₃²⁻ and M-O respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The vibration peaks at 3439, 1631, 1383 and 689 cm⁻¹ were observed, which can be assigned to -OH, H₂O, CO₃²⁻ and M-O, respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: Weight loss in two stages: 40-150°C for interlayer/adsorbed H₂O, 150-425°C for -OH and CO₃²⁻ elimination with LDH-to-spinel transition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the weight loss mode can be separated into two stages. The one in the range from 40°C to 150°C corresponds to the evaporation of H₂O of the interlayer and adsorbed water molecules, while the other in the range from 150°C to 425°C is the elimination of the -OH and CO₃²⁻ from the interlayer

nodes.characterization_summary: Peaks at 452 and 536 cm⁻¹ assigned to Ni-O vibrations of defective/disordered Niᴵᴵ-O, 294 cm⁻¹ to Feᴵᴵᴵ-O species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the peaks at 452 and 536 cm⁻¹ could be assigned to Ni-O vibrations of defective or disordered Niᴵᴵ-O, while the characteristic peak at 294 cm⁻¹ is associated with the existence of Feᴵᴵᴵ-O species

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p: peaks at ~856.2 eV (2p3/2), 873.8 eV (2p1/2), satellites 861.8/880.0 eV, Ni³⁺ 66% in Ni0.3Fe0.7-LDH@NF; Fe 2p: ~712.6 eV (2p3/2), 725.6 eV (2p1/2), satellites 721.8/734.8 eV confirming Fe³⁺; O 1s: ~529.8 eV (M-O), 531.4 eV (M-OH), 532.5 eV (Ov), 533.3 eV (H2O) with higher Ov content in Ni0.3Fe0.7-LDH@NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2b presents the high-resolution curves of the Ni 2p spectra, demonstrating two dominant peaks at binding energies of ∼856.2 eV and 873.8 eV... the Ni0.3Fe0.7 LDH@NF features the highest percentage of Ni³⁺ (66.00%)... Fe 2p spectra... ∼712.6 and 725.6 eV... validating the Fe 2p3/2 and Fe 2p1/2 of Fe³⁺... O 1 s spectra... ∼529.8, 531.4, 532.5 and 533.3 eV are attributed to lattice oxygen (M-O), hydroxide (M-OH), oxygen vacancies (Ov) and surface-adsorbed H2O

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES shows higher oxidation state for Ni0.3Fe0.7-LDH@NF; EXAFS: Ni-O at 1.59 Å, Ni-Ni/Fe at 2.72 Å; Fe K-edge: Fe-O CN=5.1 at 1.56 Å for Ni0.3Fe0.7-LDH@NF indicating highest Ov and metal vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the normalized Ni-K X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectrum presents that the oxidation state of Ni0.3Fe0.7-LDH@NF is higher... the peaks at 1.59 Å and 2.72 Å... first shell Ni-O and... second shell Ni-Ni/Fe... Ni0.3Fe0.7-LDH@NF reflects a lowest CN (5.1) of Fe-O at the dominant peak of 1.56 Å
the signal intensity of electron spin resonance (ESR) (Fig. 3i) at the g values of ~2.11 and 2.23 also demonstrates the presence of O_v and Ni³⁺, respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: C_dl = 6.66 mF·cm⁻² for Ni₀.₃Fe₀.₇-LDH@NF; b-values 0.816 (anodic) and 0.802 (cathodic); 65.19% pseudocapacitive contribution at 5 mV·s⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the C_dl of Ni₀.₃Fe₀.₇-LDH@NF is determined to be 6.66 mF·cm⁻²... 65.19% of the redox current arises from the pseudocapacitive contribution
the charge transfer resistance (R_ct) of Ni₀.₃Fe₀.₇-LDH@NF is the lowest (9.479 Ω·cm² @200 mV)
